overview: Computer Vision enables machines to interpret and understand visual information. This module covers image representation fundamentals and image classification — the foundational CV task.
Understanding how computers 'see' images is essential before building vision models. We explore color models, image formats, preprocessing, and the complete classification pipeline.

topics.title: Image Representation
theory: Digital images are 3D tensors of shape (Height, Width, Channels). A 1920×1080 RGB image has shape (1080, 1920, 3) with 6.2 million values.
RGB color model: each pixel has Red, Green, Blue values 0-255. White=(255,255,255), Black=(0,0,0). Grayscale uses single channel with weighted average: Gray = 0.299R + 0.587G + 0.114B.
Other color spaces: HSV (Hue, Saturation, Value) — better for color-based segmentation. LAB (Lightness, A, B) — perceptually uniform. YCbCr — used in JPEG compression.
Normalization: Scale 0-255 to 0-1 for neural networks. Standardization: (x - mean) / std for zero mean, unit variance. Critical for model training.
visualIntuition: Interactive pixel explorer: hover to see RGB values. Channel separation showing R, G, B as separate grayscale images. 3D tensor visualization.
visualSuggestions: Color space converter with live preview
Resolution pyramid showing quality vs size tradeoff

topics.title: Image Preprocessing
theory: Resizing: Neural networks often require fixed input size (e.g., 224×224). Methods: nearest neighbor (fast, blocky), bilinear (smooth), bicubic (highest quality).
Data augmentation artificially expands training data: random flips, rotations, crops, brightness/contrast changes. Reduces overfitting and improves generalization.
Batch processing: Images processed in batches for efficiency. Tensor shape becomes (Batch, Height, Width, Channels) — e.g., (32, 224, 224, 3).
File formats: JPEG (lossy, smaller files), PNG (lossless, larger), TIFF (professional). Bit depth: 8-bit (256 levels) standard, 16-bit for medical/scientific.
visualIntuition: Augmentation showcase: original image surrounded by augmented versions (flipped, rotated, color-jittered).

code.content:
from tensorflow.keras.preprocessing.image import ImageDataGenerator
import cv2

# Resize image
resized = cv2.resize(img, (224, 224), interpolation=cv2.INTER_AREA)

# Data augmentation generator
datagen = ImageDataGenerator(
    rotation_range=15,
    horizontal_flip=True,
    width_shift_range=0.1,
    height_shift_range=0.1,
    brightness_range=[0.8, 1.2],
    zoom_range=0.1
)

# Generate augmented versions
img_batch = img.reshape(1, *img.shape)  # Add batch dimension
augmented = datagen.flow(img_batch, batch_size=1)

topics.title: Image Classification Pipeline
theory: Classification assigns a label from predefined categories to an entire image. Input: image tensor. Output: probability distribution over classes.
Pipeline: Input → Preprocessing (resize, normalize) → Feature Extraction (CNN layers) → Classification (dense + softmax) → Output probabilities.
Loss function: Categorical cross-entropy measures prediction error. For true class c with predicted probability p_c: Loss = -log(p_c). Punishes confident wrong predictions.
Common architectures: Simple CNN (for learning), VGG (simple but many params), ResNet (deep with skip connections), MobileNet (efficient), EfficientNet (state-of-art).
visualIntuition: Classification pipeline animation: image flows through network layers, feature maps shown, final bar chart of class probabilities.

code.content:
from tensorflow import keras
from tensorflow.keras import layers, models

def build_classifier(input_shape=(224, 224, 3), num_classes=10):
    model = models.Sequential([
        # Feature extraction
        layers.Conv2D(32, (3, 3), activation='relu', padding='same', input_shape=input_shape),
        layers.BatchNormalization(),
        layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)),
        layers.Conv2D(64, (3, 3), activation='relu', padding='same'),
        layers.BatchNormalization(),
        layers.MaxPooling2D((2, 2)),
        layers.Conv2D(128, (3, 3), activation='relu', padding='same'),
        layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D(),
        
        # Classification
        layers.Dense(256, activation='relu'),
        layers.Dropout(0.5),
        layers.Dense(num_classes, activation='softmax')
    ])
    
    model.compile(
        optimizer='adam',
        loss='categorical_crossentropy',
        metrics=['accuracy']
    )
    return model

topics.title: Evaluation and Metrics
theory: Accuracy: Correct predictions / Total predictions. Misleading for imbalanced classes. Use balanced accuracy or per-class metrics.
Confusion matrix: N×N table for N classes. Entry (i,j) = count of class i predicted as j. Reveals which classes are confused.
Precision (per class): Of predicted positives, how many are correct? Recall: Of actual positives, how many found? F1: Harmonic mean of precision and recall.
Top-K accuracy: True label in top K predictions? Essential for large class sets (ImageNet: 1000 classes, Top-5 used).
visualIntuition: Interactive confusion matrix heatmap. Click cell to see example misclassified images.
visualSuggestions: t-SNE/UMAP feature visualization colored by class

topics.title: Transfer Learning
theory: Training from scratch requires massive data and compute. Transfer learning leverages pretrained models (trained on ImageNet with 1.2M images).
Process: Load pretrained model → Remove final classification layer → Add new layer for your classes → Fine-tune on your data.
Feature extraction: Freeze pretrained layers, only train new classification head. Fast, works with small datasets.
Fine-tuning: Unfreeze some/all pretrained layers, train with low learning rate. Better accuracy but needs more data. Risk of catastrophic forgetting.
visualIntuition: Pretrained network with locked layers (blue) and trainable classifier (green). Data flowing through frozen feature extractor.

code.content:
from tensorflow.keras.applications import ResNet50
from tensorflow.keras import layers, models

# Load pretrained ResNet50 (without top classification layer)
base_model = ResNet50(weights='imagenet', include_top=False, input_shape=(224, 224, 3))

# Freeze pretrained layers
base_model.trainable = False

# Add custom classification head
model = models.Sequential([
    base_model,
    layers.GlobalAveragePooling2D(),
    layers.Dense(256, activation='relu'),
    layers.Dropout(0.5),
    layers.Dense(num_classes, activation='softmax')
])

model.compile(optimizer='adam', loss='categorical_crossentropy', metrics=['accuracy'])

# Train only the new layers
model.fit(train_data, epochs=10)

# Optional: Fine-tune by unfreezing some layers
base_model.trainable = True
for layer in base_model.layers[:-20]:  # Freeze all except last 20 layers
    layer.trainable = False

model.compile(optimizer=keras.optimizers.Adam(1e-5), loss='categorical_crossentropy')
